messages:
maria (eng-platform): heads up — us-west2-a GPU pending is spiking, ~120 pods Pending with small GPU requests. I think this is the slot-mosaic problem again, small pods scattered across racks and taints preventing coalescing.
jon (eng-infra): can you paste the pending histogram? suspect tiny-pod islanding + a few tainted racks.
maria (eng-platform): pasted a snippet: `pending_by_size: { tiny: 83, small: 27, medium: 10 }` and `rack_taints: r1: 14, r2: 9` — warm pools are healthy, but packing isn't consolidating.
tess (eng-sre): saw elevated eviction churn too — preemptions failing because preempt-window > scheduling latency, ends up requeueing same pods. net egress in that AZ had a conntrack spike last hour. could be compounding.
ash: @ashley any recent network flaps in us-west2-a? (sorry wrong handle, meant ashley)
ashley (eng-runtime): yeah we had a conntrack surge on a subset of nodes — logs show `netfilter: conntrack table full` on two racks for ~12m. kube-proxy lagged, so some binds failed which may've left leases orphaned. cc: schedulers.
scheduler-bot: US-WEST2-A: GPU_pending=120 (+42 in 15m), avg_pack_util=62%, hot_rack_skew=0.42. Tagged nodes with conntrack alerts.
jon (eng-infra): plan proposal: 1) run targeted descheduler job for tiny pods with `--threshold=0.15` to force consolidation across racks, 2) reduce `preempt-window` from 30s->12s for a canary rollout in us-west2-a, 3) increase warm-pool ephemeral size +3 for 30m to absorb latency while resync runs.
ryan (oncall): I can kick the descheduler in 10m on the canary label `usw2a-mosaic-canary`. schedule: descheduler now, then patch preempt-window at +20m if we see reduced churn.
maria (eng-platform): can we avoid global scheduler rollout? do per-az flagging. also cost note: consolidation may raise short-term spot churn — finance flagged a spike last month when we did a wide deschedule.
jon (eng-infra): yep per-az flag only. I'll prepare a kustomize overlay for the scheduler config with `preempt-window: 12s` and `nodeAffinityRelax: tiny` for batch pods -> temporary.
tess (eng-sre): add smoke tests: 1) validate pending count drops under 30 within 25m, 2) eviction rate down by 40%, 3) no new conntrack errors. If not met, rollback.
ashley (eng-runtime): ops note: I'm increasing conntrack max to 524288 on the two affected racks now; will monitor for 10m.
ryan (oncall): descheduler kicked — running `kubectl apply -f descheduler-tiny-rescue.yaml --namespace kube-system --selector=usw2a-mosaic-canary`
maria (eng-platform): thanks. tagging owners: @jon -> infra changes, @ryan -> descheduler job, @ashley -> conntrack tweak, @tess -> rollout gating.
jon (eng-infra): ack. will push overlay once descheduler results in 15m.
tess (eng-sre): watching metrics. if pending stalls, we'll also try a quick `node-evict` of the 9 low-util tainted nodes as last resort. small step, not whole-rack drain.
maria (eng-platform): update: after descheduler run pending dropped to 38, pack_util -> 78%, eviction spike down. preliminary win. leaving this thread open to decide preempt-window patch. :thumbsup:
ryan (oncall): confirmed metrics steady. I'm keeping the descheduler run for another 10m, then will snapshot and shut it down.
jon (eng-infra): pulling the kustomize overlay now, will stage preempt-window canary with traffic shaping.
tess (eng-sre): if canary looks good @30m, we can roll az-by-az. otherwise rollback to 30s.
maria (eng-platform): thanks team — good quick sync. follow-up: file a short postmortem note if we had cost impact > $750 in this incident.
ryan (oncall): will create follow-up thread with numbers.
maria (eng-platform): closing for now, moving to monitoring-only. :white_check_mark:
